The K dimension is walked in\n// tiles of BK, staged through shared memory. Within each thread the products\n// are accumulated in strictly ascending k order, exactly as in the sequential\n// reference, so the numerical result is the same as the original algorithm.\nconstexpr int BM = 64;   // block tile rows\nconstexpr int BN = 64;   // block tile cols\nconstexpr int BK = 16;   // K-tile depth\nconstexpr int TDIM = 16; // threads per block dimension\nconstexpr int TM = BM / TDIM; // 4 outputs per thread along rows\nconstexpr int TN = BN / TDIM; // 4 outputs per thread along cols\n\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(TDIM * TDIM)\nmatmulKernel(const double* __restrict__ A, const double* __restrict__ B,\n             double* __restrict__ C, const size_t N) {\n    // As is stored transposed (k-major) and padded to avoid shared-memory bank conflicts.\n    __shared__ double As[BK][BM + 1];\n    __shared__ double Bs[BK][BN];\n\n    const int tx = threadIdx.x;\n    const int ty = threadIdx.y;\n    const int tid = ty * TDIM + tx;\n    constexpr int NTHREADS = TDIM * TDIM;\n\n    const size_t rowBase = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.y) * BM;\n    const size_t colBase = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * BN;\n\n    double acc[TM][TN];\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int i = 0; i < TM; ++i)\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int j = 0; j < TN; ++j)\n            acc[i][j] = 0.0;\n\n    for (size_t k0 = 0; k0 < N; k0 += BK) {\n        // Load A tile (BM x BK) into As[kk][row]; zero-pad out-of-range entries.\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int r = 0; r < (BM * BK) / NTHREADS; ++r) {\n            const int idx = tid + r * NTHREADS;\n            const int row = idx / BK;\n            const int kk = idx % BK;\n            const size_t gRow = rowBase + row;\n            const size_t gK = k0 + kk;\n            As[kk][row] = (gRow < N && gK < N) ? A[gRow * N + gK] : 0.0;\n        }\n        // Load B tile (BK x BN) into Bs[kk][col]; zero-pad out-of-range entries.\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int r = 0; r < (BK * BN) / NTHREADS; ++r) {\n            const int idx = tid + r * NTHREADS;\n            const int kk = idx / BN;\n            const int col = idx % BN;\n            const size_t gK = k0 + kk;\n            const size_t gCol = colBase + col;\n            Bs[kk][col] = (gK < N && gCol < N) ? B[gK * N + gCol] : 0.0;\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int kk = 0; kk < BK; ++kk) {\n            double a[TM];\n            double b[TN];\n#pragma unroll\n            for (int i = 0; i < TM; ++i)\n                a[i] = As[kk][ty + TDIM * i];\n#pragma unroll\n            for (int j = 0; j < TN; ++j)\n                b[j] = Bs[kk][tx + TDIM * j];\n#pragma unroll\n            for (int i = 0; i < TM; ++i)\n#pragma unroll\n                for (int j = 0; j < TN; ++j)\n                    acc[i][j] += a[i] * b[j];\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int i = 0; i < TM; ++i) {\n        const size_t gRow = rowBase + ty + TDIM * i;\n        if (gRow >= N) continue;\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int j = 0; j < TN; ++j) {\n            const size_t gCol = colBase + tx + TDIM * j;\n            if (gCol < N) {\n                C[gRow * N + gCol] = acc[i][j];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Multiply A * B on the GPU. Inputs and output are host vectors; device buffers\n// are allocated, transferred, computed and released within this call.\nvoid matrixMultiply(const std::vector<double>& A, const std::vector<double>& B,\n                    std::vector<double>& C, const size_t N) {\n    if (N == 0) return;\n\n    const size_t bytes = N * N * sizeof(double);\n    double *dA = nullptr, *dB = nullptr, *dC = nullptr;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dA, bytes));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dB, bytes));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dC, bytes));\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dA, A.data(), bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dB, B.data(), bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n\n    const dim3 block(TDIM, TDIM);\n    const dim3 grid(static_cast<unsigned int>((N + BN - 1) / BN),\n                    static_cast<unsigned int>((N + BM - 1) / BM));\n    matmulKernel<<<grid, block>>>(dA, dB, dC, N);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(C.data(), dC, bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dA));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dB));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dC));\n}\n\n// Simple validation: compute a single element and compare\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<double>& A, const std::vector<double>& B,\n                   const std::vector<double>& C, const size_t N) {\n    // Check a few random positions\n    constexpr size_t checkPoints[] = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4};\n    \n    for (size_t pi = 0; pi < 5; ++pi) {\n        for (size_t pj = 0; pj < 5; ++pj) {\n            const size_t i = checkPoints[pi] % N;\n            const size_t j = checkPoints[pj] % N;\n            \n            double expected = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < N; ++k) {\n                expected += A[i * N + k] * B[k * N + j];\n            }\n            \n            const double actual = C[i * N + j];\n            const double relError = std::abs((actual - expected) / (expected + 1e-10));\n            \n            if (relError > 1e-6) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at (%zu, %zu): expected %.10f, got %.10f (error: %.10e)\\n\",\n                       i, j, expected, actual, relError);\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size N (computes NxN * NxN) (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t N = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            N = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) }\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Matrix Multiplication Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Matrix size: %zu x %zu\\n\", N, N);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    \n print_results(C, \"MatrixC\");\n    }\n    \n    // Validation\n    if (validate) {\n        printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n        bool valid = validateResult(A, B, C, N);\n        \n That's puzzling since the initialization and loop structure should produce identical fused operations on both platforms, so there must be some other source of divergence I'm not accounting for yet.\n\nGiven that, I'm narrowing down the real decision for shipping: either keep nvcc's default FMA contraction for speed, accepting small floating-point differences from the original CPU reference that still fall within the validation tolerance, or disable FMA entirely so the GPU matches the strict, non-contracted CPU reference bit-for-bit at a modest performance cost.\n\nChecking the actual numbers, the GPU sum versus the non-FMA reference only diverges at the relative 1e-16 level, which is just ordinary rounding noise—nothing alarming. The deeper discrepancy between GPU-fused and CPU-fused results likely comes down to GCC potentially contracting the multiply-add with a different operand ordering than the GPU does, since multiplication is commutative but floating-point rounding isn't.\n\nI'm not going to chase this further by digging into disassembly—it's not worth the time given the small magnitude of the difference.
